evals.prompt: Generate a client so our React frontend can call the export-quote-pdf Edge Function. It's already built on Hono + zod-openapi.
evals.expected_output: Fetches the function's OpenAPI spec, adds openapi-typescript and openapi-fetch to the frontend's package.json, generates a types file into an existing (or newly picked) API-client location, builds a thin openapi-fetch client wrapper whose middleware pulls the current Supabase session JWT per request, and commits both the generated types and the wrapper.
expectations: Identifies the consumer as the browser frontend and the auth model as a Supabase session JWT before generating anything
Fetches the OpenAPI spec from the function's spec route (local dev server or deployed URL)
Adds openapi-typescript and openapi-fetch to the frontend's package.json, not the target function's deno.json
Checks for an existing API-client folder convention before picking an output path
Generated client's fetch middleware pulls the Supabase session JWT per request rather than caching it once
States that both the generated types file and the client wrapper get committed, not gitignored

evals.prompt: The generate-invoice function needs to call export-quote-pdf directly, server-to-server. export-quote-pdf already verifies a shared secret from an env var. Generate a client for this.
evals.expected_output: Identifies generate-invoice (another Edge Function) as the consumer with shared-secret auth, adds openapi-fetch as an npm: specifier to generate-invoice's own supabase/functions/deno.json (not export-quote-pdf's), keeps openapi-typescript as a dev-time-only Node/npm step whose output is portable into Deno, and builds a client whose middleware reads the shared secret from an environment variable and sets it on the header export-quote-pdf's handler checks.
expectations: Identifies the consumer as another Edge Function with shared-secret (not Supabase-session) auth
Adds openapi-fetch as an npm: specifier to generate-invoice's deno.json import map, not export-quote-pdf's
Treats openapi-typescript as a dev-time-only generator whose plain .ts output is portable into Deno, without trying to run the generator itself inside Deno
Client middleware reads the shared secret from an environment variable (Deno.env.get or equivalent) and sets it on the header the target handler checks
Does not apply a constant-time comparison in the client — that requirement is called out as belonging to the receiving handler, not the caller

evals.prompt: Regenerate the client for export-quote-pdf — I think the response shape changed. There's already a generated types file and client wrapper from before.
evals.expected_output: Notices the existing generated types file and client wrapper, tells the user they already exist, and asks whether to regenerate before overwriting anything — doesn't silently skip since the user just said the spec changed, and doesn't silently overwrite without flagging that a file is being replaced.
expectations: Detects that a types file and/or client wrapper already exists at the expected output location before running codegen
Surfaces to the user that existing generated output was found rather than silently overwriting or silently leaving it alone
Asks (or confirms via the prompt's own stated intent) whether to regenerate, given the user already indicated the spec changed
Proceeds to regenerate only after that's settled, not automatically on detecting existing files

evals.prompt: Generate a client for the legacy-webhook function so another service can call it.
evals.expected_output: Checks whether legacy-webhook is built on Hono + zod-openapi; if it's still raw Deno.serve with no OpenAPI spec, stops and recommends moving it to Hono + zod-openapi via the create-edge-function skill first, rather than hand-typing a response shape from the handler code.
expectations: Checks whether the target function actually serves an OpenAPI spec before attempting to generate anything
If no spec exists, stops and recommends the create-edge-function skill's Hono + zod-openapi step rather than proceeding
Does not hand-type a response shape by reading the handler's code as a substitute for a real spec
